lxc_da571217d8b4c4e5.text: The dates work as expected only when you store the food correctly.

lxc_523b7fe0cdb19476.text: The packet may say “keep refrigerated” or “store in a cool, dry place.

lxc_fba0f2de50316297.text: ” It may also tell you what to do after you open it.

lxc_8a1ef528349942d5.text: For example, a chilled food can become unsafe before its use-by date if you leave it out of the fridge.

lxc_7497a64b7ade31c3.text: Dried food can lose quality early if it gets wet.

lxc_36cb7a0b5c231d83.text: Read the storage instructions every time, and follow them.

lxc_5bacf01cac08bbef.text: If you cannot eat food before its use-by date, you may be able to cook or freeze it in time.

lxc_265cf19556769fc2.text: You can freeze food on or before the use-by date.

lxc_bdae92c61fb3dad0.text: Keep the freezer at −18°C and follow the packet’s freezing and defrosting instructions.

lxc_747d12fd80f0e082.text: After you defrost the food, use it within 24 hours.

lxc_9c90632d9f4a5a2e.text: You can also cook food on or before the date.

lxc_9f75e2c533add84b.text: Cool it, keep it in the fridge, and eat it within 48 hours, or freeze it.

lxc_b9b1fd7fbc2fbcfb.text: For example, if raw chicken has a use-by date of Tuesday and you cannot cook it by then, freeze it on Monday or Tuesday—not Wednesday.

occurrences.surface: store in a cool, dry place
